chapter: Reel 2: Los Angeles musicians, the Apex and Cotton Club
title: Charlie Lawrence, the schooled pianist
summary: Howard praises Charlie Lawrence as a studious pianist who played everything, including Rhapsody in Blue and After Hours, and whom Lloyd Reese admired.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: What about another we were talking about him before, Charlie Lawrence.
Charlie Lawrence?
Yeah, piano player.
He played with me.
He did, huh?
Yeah. Oh, my, he played his head off.
He was a good piano player.
You ought to get him started playing Rhapsody in Blue. He would play, boy.
Yeah. Well, what's his background? Was he studying here a lot? He was the kind of guy that was studying all the time.
Studied all the time.
That's the guy who Lloyd Reese always used (Inaudible) to talk about.
He was the guy that Lloyd -- Lloyd took
after him. Yeah, Charlie Lawrence.
He seemed to be the schooled pianist around at the time.
He was very, very, very good.
You know, (inaudible) the fingers, left hand, right hand.
Yeah, he was a very good pianist.
He was a good jazz pianist, too, eh?

Yeah, played everything, and played like the devil. I'm trying to think what -- I'd make him play -- get him to play -- what do you call that? Not the Birth of the Blues, but -- oh, he used to play some blues. What's the name of that tune that everybody played and tried to learn to play here?
Not the (inaudible)? Avery Parnish Thing, was it?
No.
"After Hours"?
"After Hours", yeah, he played that.
Charlie used to play that. And then he played another one, a good one, too.
I see him every now and then. He must live near me. I see him in Depart (inaudible). Restaurant
You do, huh? Well, he's there.
Yeah, he's close, on Wilshire or something.
Yep, he's there.
